title: Grateful Dead Live at Fieldhouse, University of Iowa on 1973-02-24

ai_review.summary: Stunning soundboard capture of Phil's legendary 1973 bass solo – crystal‑clear treble, crunchy stereo bass and a smoking jam.
ai_review.review: This fragment from the February 24 1973 show delivers one of the most exhilarating Phil Lesh moments ever recorded. Reviewers rave about the pristine soundboard mix that showcases an almost three‑dimensional bass tone, while the musical flow – Truckin' into Nobody's Fault and spilling into a “groovy” jam that leads toward Sugar Magnolia – is described as pure fire. The only downside noted is the short length of the available excerpt.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly enthusiastic reviews (majority 5‑star) praise both the musical performance and the high‑fidelity soundboard recording; minor criticism is limited to fragment length, not quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp treble, crunchy bass with remarkable stereo separation that captures the Wall‑of‑Sound effect; reviewers note the mix is clear and “HQ”, though only a 9‑minute fragment is available.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fragment sits between Truckin' and the segue into Sugar Magnolia, building a tight, high‑energy jam that highlights Phil’s solo before moving forward.

band_member_comments.Phil: Repeatedly praised for an "awesome" bass tone, stereo spread, and powerful solo – described as the highlight of the recording.
